#### Syllabus and Class Notes

| Unit              | Syllabus                         |       Vibha's Notes                |
| :---------------- | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| Unit 1            | - Mathematical Preliminaries <br> - Basic Notations <br> - Deterministic Finite Acceptors (DFA) <br> - Non-Deterministic Finite Acceptors (NFA) <br> - $\lambda$-NFA (Lambda-NFA) <br> - Equivalence of Deterministic and Non-deterministic <br> Finite Acceptors <br> - Reduction of the number of states in Finite Automata <br> (Minimization of DFA)          | [AFLL Unit 1.pdf](AFLL%20Unit%201.pdf) |
| Unit 2            | - Regular Expressions <br> - Connection between Regular Expressions Regular Languages <br> - Regular Grammars <br> - Properties of Regular Languages <br> - Pumping Lemma and identifying Non–Regular Languages | [AFLL Unit 2.pdf](AFLL%20Unit%202.pdf) |
| Unit 3            | - Context Free Grammars <br> - Parsing and Ambiguity <br> - Formal Definitions of Pushdown Automata <br> - Deterministic Pushdown Automata <br> - Non Deterministic Pushdown Automata <br> - Methods for Transforming Grammars <br> - Two important Normal Forms <br> - A Membership Algorithm for Context–Free Languages <br> - Pushdown down Automata and Context Free Languages   | [AFLL Unit 3.pdf](AFLL%20Unit%203.pdf) |
| Unit 4            | - Properties of Context–Free Languages <br> - Pumping Lemma for Context–Free Languages <br> - The Standard Turing Machine <br> - Combining Turing Machine for Complicated Tasks <br> - Turing Thesis <br> - Recursive and Recursively Enumerable Languages <br> - Context Sensitive Grammar and Languages <br> - The Chomsky Hierarchy <br> - Some Problems that Cannot be solved by Turing Machine <br> - PCP <br> - Undecidable Problems for Recursively Enumerable Languages  | [AFLL Unit 4.pdf](AFLL%20Unit%204.pdf) |
| Unit 5            | - Propositional Logic: A very simple logic <br> - Syntax <br> - Semantics <br> - A simple knowledge Base <br> - A simple Inference procedure <br> - Inferences and Proofs <br> - Proof by resolution <br> - First Order Logic: Syntax and Semantics of First <br> order logic <br> - Numbers, Sets and Lists <br> - Example - The electronic circuit Domain   | [AFLL Unit 5.pdf](AFLL%20Unit%205.pdf) |


<br>


#### Textbooks: 

-  **T1**: "An Introduction to Formal Languages and Automata", Peter Linz, Jones and Bartlett, New Delhi, India, 5th Edition, 2011
-  **T2**: "Artificial Intelligence – A Modern Approach", Stuart Russell and Peter Norvig, Pearson, 3rd Edition (Paperback), 2016

<br>

#### Reference Books:

- **R1**: "Theory of Computation", Michael Sipser, Cengage Learning, New Delhi, India, 2008
- **R2**: "Introduction to Automata Theory, Languages, and Computation", John E Hopcroft, Rajeev Motwani, Jeffrey D Ullman, Pearson Education, New Delhi, India, 3rd Edition, 2009
- **R3**: "Theory of Computation: A Problem–Solving Approach", Kavi Mahesh, Wiley India, New Delhi, 2012
